requirement:
When authoring evidence for a named example, its complete fenced declaration
MUST be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
**Obligation.** When the subject of an assessment is a named example, the example's complete fenced declaration MUST be in the mandatory input set. The declaration runs from the `:::{example} name` opening fence to the closing `:::`. The rest of the mandatory-input mechanics (combining contributions, deduplication, `evidence/` exclusion, and so on) belong to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, which is cited here as context. I did not reassess them.

**Test coverage.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` runs `AssessmentSources::prepare(root, "requirements.case")` on an example declaration.
  - It asserts that `subject_kind` is `AssessmentKind::Definition(DefinitionKind::Example, false)`.
  - It asserts that the first mandatory input has `requirements == "requirements.case"`.
  - It asserts that the input's `text` is exactly the full declaration: the `:::{example} case` opening line, the body line carrying the `{cite}` and `{test}` roles, and the closing `:::`.
  - That is an exact-equality check on the whole fenced declaration, including both fences. A truncated declaration, or one missing a fence, would fail it.
  - When the subject is the requirement `requirements.ready`, the same test also checks that the example `requirements.case` is included as a mandatory input, because it carries a `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to the subject.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]` runs through `:::{example} case` declarations whose body contains several citation roles.
  - It asserts that `sources.subject_text` contains the full citation text.
  - It asserts that some mandatory input's joined `text` contains that same citation text.
  - This shows the example's body, including its citation metadata, reaches the mandatory input set intact, even though the book display hides it.

**Gaps.** I found none. The requirement states one obligation and has no distinct modes. Both tests are marked with `{test}` references to `requirements.examples.authoring_inputs`. The assertions check the content of the example's input, not merely that the code ran.
